source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Document the date, time, location, and details of the inspection.
3. Identify the specific areas or systems where compliance was lacking.
4. List all the failed regulations, including reference to the specific codes or standards (e.g., NFPA 101, IBC, etc.)
5. Photograph non-compliant issues with timestamps and detailed captions.
6. Note the personnel conducting the inspection and any witnesses or additional observers present.
7. Record the name and contact information of the person/entity responsible for the building maintenance and safety.
8. For each failed item, describe why it failed (e.g., missing fire extinguisher, blocked exits, non-working fire alarms).
9. Indicate if any immediate hazards pose a risk to occupants and whether any emergency action was required (e.g., evacuation).
10. Write concise, objective descriptions of issues, avoiding personal opinions or non-pertinent information.
11. Include any verbal feedback or instructions given to property management
